newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CBA PLANS ASSET MANAGEMENT BUSINESS GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: CBA PLANS ASSET MANAGEMENT BUSINESS GROWTH.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) said on Thursday it was looking at expanding its asset management business and had list of opportunities.

"We have a range of items on the list at the moment. We have had a list there for a long time, but we have to have regard for price and conditions that fit with our business," Murray told reporters after he addressed a luncheon on the bank's full year results which were released on Wednesday.
Asked what the bank could afford by way of expansion in this area, Murray said: "If the return is good enough plenty. That is what our investors want us to do."
In his earlier speech, Murray said the bank expected that non-bank financial intermediation would continue to grow at 1.5 times the rate of bank intermediation.

"That's why we are very interested in asset management. That's why we have made a couple of acquisitions in the last twelve months to improve our position. We continue to be targeting a rapid build-up in asset management," Murray said.
Late last year CBA bought Australia's second largest funds manager, Commonwealth Funds Management, from the Federal government for an undisclosed amount.
